newsitem.title: UK: Dinosaur egg project faces extinction.
newsitem.headline: Dinosaur egg project faces extinction.

text.p: A team of British scientists who have what they think are the best-preserved dinosaur eggs in the world said on Thursday they feared their project might fall apart after failing to sell some of their eggs at auction.

The Dinosaur Embryo Project, dedicated to preserving and examining the eggs, had tried to sell off two of its precious eggs to fund further research, but they failed to reach their reserve price of $80,000 apiece at a New York auction on Sunday.
"We didn't get one bid. Nothing went down," said Terry Manning, a fossil restorer and collector who heads the project.
"I'm at a loss to think why we didn't get any overseas bidders...(but) I'm glad they didn't sell for nothing."

The two eggs, found in China, were from the same nest. They have been identified as belonging to a therizinosaur, a two-legged dinosaur that lived in the Upper Cretaceous period, 75 million years ago.
Manning said the project was already badly strapped and may fall apart if some other funding is not found. "I'm worried about losing the project now," he said.

Manning bought the clutch eggs, seven in total, from a freelance trader in 1992, and developed unique methods for examining and preserving them. He found the egg yolk well-preserved -- something never seen in a dinosaur egg before.
"These embryos that I have are indeed the best in the world," he said.
He said the embryos inside also seemed to have shed several sets of teeth before hatching and said more research might shed light on how and why this would happen.
Now he hopes a university will take on the collection so research by his collaborators, who include palaeontologists and other experts, can continue.
Until that happens or someone makes a donation or buys the eggs, the scientists cannot continue their work.
